title: Crabs in Tomato-Based Sauce, Puerto Rican Style

content.title: About
content.content: Crabs in tomato-based sauce, Puerto Rican style, is a dish made from fresh crab meat simmered in a fragrant tomato sauce enriched with onion, garlic, sweet pepper, olive oil, and characteristic Puerto Rican spices such as adobo, oregano, and cumin. The dish balances the natural sweetness of the crab with a bright, slightly spicy tomato base.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Puerto Rican sauce is built on tomatoes, vinegar, and an adobo spice blend.
Puerto Rico often uses local blue crab (Callinectes sapidus) for this recipe.
The dish is commonly served with rice, beans, and "pan con queso" bread.
Puerto Rican tomato sauces frequently contain a pinch of sugar to tame acidity.
Some authentic versions add a splash of coconut milk for extra smoothness.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Crab meat provides high‑quality marine protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafood options, crab contains very little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in zinc and selenium
items.content: These minerals support immune function and act as antioxidants.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Crabs are a good source of vitamin B12, important for nervous system health and blood formation.

items.title: Lycopene from tomatoes
items.content: The tomato sauce supplies lycopene, a powerful antioxidant linked to reduced cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to crab, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Crab meat contains cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor portion size.

items.title: Heavy metals
items.content: In certain regions crabs can accumulate cadmium or mercury; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Added salt
items.content: Tomato sauce often includes added salt; those watching sodium intake may want to reduce it.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, typically alongside boiled rice, beans, or crusty bread. Crab can be eaten straight from the sauce with a fork or added to salads and pasta. Garnish with fresh cilantro or a squeeze of lime for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly to a rolling boil before serving to ensure safety.
